documents.title: SLA Definitions & Support Tiers
documents.summary: Service Level Agreement definitions, support tiers, and response time commitments
documents.body:
# SLA Definitions & Support Tiers

## Overview

This document defines the Service Level Agreements (SLAs) across all support tiers. All support staff must understand these commitments and escalate appropriately when a response risks breaching SLA.

## Support Tiers

| Tier | Price | Availability | Channels | Max Response Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | Free | Business hours | Email, Community | 48 hours |
| Standard | $29/user/mo | Business hours | Email, Chat | 8 hours |
| Professional | $99/user/mo | 24/5 (Mon-Fri) | Email, Chat, Phone | 2 hours |
| Enterprise | Custom | 24/7/365 | Priority Email, Chat, Phone, Dedicated CSM | 30 minutes |

## Severity Levels

### Severity 1 - Critical (System Down)
- **Definition**: Production system is down or severely impacted. All users affected. Data loss occurring.
- **Initial response**: 15 minutes (Enterprise), 30 minutes (Professional)
- **Update frequency**: Every 1 hour
- **Resolution target**: 4 hours (workaround) or 8 hours (fix)

### Severity 2 - High (Major Feature Down)
- **Definition**: Major feature unavailable for a segment of users. No workaround available. Performance severely degraded.
- **Initial response**: 30 minutes (Enterprise), 2 hours (Professional)
- **Update frequency**: Every 4 hours
- **Resolution target**: 24 hours

### Severity 3 - Medium (Partial Feature Issue)
- **Definition**: Minor feature issue. Workaround available. Performance moderately degraded.
- **Initial response**: 2 hours (Enterprise), 8 hours (Professional)
- **Update frequency**: Every 24 hours
- **Resolution target**: 72 hours

### Severity 4 - Low (Cosmetic / Question)
- **Definition**: Cosmetic issue, documentation error, general question, feature request.
- **Initial response**: 8 hours (Enterprise), 24 hours (Professional)
- **Resolution target**: Next release or 30 days

## SLA Credits

If we fail to meet the SLA targets for Severity 1 or 2 incidents, customers are eligible for service credits:

| Missed SLA | Credit |
|---|---|
| First violation in a month | 5% of monthly subscription |
| Second violation | 10% of monthly subscription |
| Third+ violation | 15% of monthly subscription |

## Escalation Contacts

| Escalation Level | Contact | Availability |
|---|---|---|
| L1 - Support Engineer | In-ticket escalation | During support hours |
| L2 - Senior Support Engineer | Phone + ticket | 24/7 (Enterprise) |
| L3 - Engineering Lead | On-call rotation | 24/7/365 |
| L4 - VP Engineering / CTO | Via CSM | Business hours |

documents.title: Common Support Scenarios - Troubleshooting Guide
documents.summary: Step-by-step troubleshooting for the most common SaaS support scenarios
documents.body:
# Common Support Scenarios - Troubleshooting Guide

## Overview

This guide covers the most common support scenarios encountered. Follow the steps in order - most issues are resolved at Step 1 or 2.

## Scenario 1: User Cannot Log In

### Symptoms
- Login page loads but credentials are rejected
- "Invalid email or password" error
- Account locked message

### Troubleshooting Steps
1. **Verify email**: Confirm the user is using the correct email (check for typos, domain changes)
2. **Password reset**: Walk through password reset flow
3. **Account status**: Check if account is active/suspended/terminated in admin panel
4. **SSO issues**: If using SSO, check identity provider status (Okta/Azure AD/Google Workspace)
5. **IP allowlisting**: Check if the user's IP is blocked or requires allowlisting
6. **Browser issues**: Clear cache/cookies, try incognito mode, try different browser
7. **Escalate**: If none of the above works, escalate to Engineering with HAR file and browser console logs

## Scenario 2: Feature Not Working / Error Message

### Symptoms
- Specific feature throws an error
- Unexpected behavior
- Error message displayed

### Troubleshooting Steps
1. **Reproduce**: Ask for exact steps, browser, OS, and environment (prod/staging)
2. **Check status page**: Is there a known incident? Check status.company.com
3. **Browser console**: Ask user to open browser console (F12) and share screenshots of errors
4. **Network tab**: Check for failed API requests (red entries in Network tab)
5. **Version check**: What version/branch are they on? Feature may not be released yet
6. **Permissions**: Verify user has the correct role/permissions for the feature
7. **Integration health**: If the feature uses a third-party integration, check integration status
8. **Escalate**: Gather logs, screenshots, recording and escalate with reproduction steps

## Scenario 3: Billing / Payment Issue

### Symptoms
- Payment declined
- Incorrect charge
- Duplicate charge
- Cannot update payment method

### Troubleshooting Steps
1. **Verify payment method**: Check if card is expired, has insufficient funds, or is blocked
2. **Check Stripe/Billing dashboard**: Look at recent transactions, failures, and webhook logs
3. **Subscription status**: Verify subscription is active and not in past_due/dunning status
4. **Invoice review**: Compare invoiced amount vs plan pricing
5. **Refund policy**: Refer to refund policy before processing any refund
6. **Manual fix**: If automated billing failed, process payment manually or issue credit
7. **Escalate**: Billing discrepancies over $500 or recurring billing bugs go to Finance

## Scenario 4: Performance / Slow Load Times

### Symptoms
- Pages load slowly
- API calls timeout
- Spinner shows for extended periods

### Troubleshooting Steps
1. **Is it widespread?** Check status page and internal monitoring dashboards
2. **User's connection**: Ask the user to run a speed test and share results
3. **Geography**: Check if the user is far from the nearest CDN edge
4. **Browser**: Test in a different browser or incognito mode
5. **Ad blockers / extensions**: Ask to disable browser extensions
6. **VPN**: Check if using VPN that routes traffic through a congested endpoint
7. **Escalate**: If isolated to a specific region or time, escalate to Engineering with tracing data

## Scenario 5: Data Export / Import Issues

### Symptoms
- Export fails or times out
- Import fails with validation errors
- Exported data incomplete

### Troubleshooting Steps
1. **Data volume**: Very large exports may time out - suggest smaller date ranges
2. **File format**: Verify the requested export format is supported
3. **Import validation**: Check the import file for common issues (wrong columns, encoding, date format)
4. **Row limits**: Check if there's a row limit on imports
5. **Template**: Provide the correct import template and ask them to reformat
6. **Escalate**: Persistent import failures with valid data go to Engineering

documents.title: Escalation Paths & Incident Management
documents.summary: Defined escalation paths, incident severity classification, and incident response procedures
documents.body:
# Escalation Paths & Incident Management

## Overview

Clear escalation paths ensure issues reach the right team quickly. This document defines the escalation hierarchy, incident severity classification, and incident response procedures.

## Escalation Hierarchy


Customer -> L1 Support Engineer
                |
                +--> L2 Senior Support Engineer
                        |
                        +--> L3 Engineering Lead (technical bugs)
                        +--> L3 Product Manager (feature gaps)
                        +--> L3 Billing Team (billing issues)
                |
                +--> Customer Success Manager (relationship escalations)


## When to Escalate

### Escalate to L2 When:
- Issue not resolved after 2 hours of troubleshooting
- Requires access to server logs or database queries
- Customer is visibly frustrated and L1 has exhausted options
- Potential security or data privacy concern identified

### Escalate to L3 (Engineering) When:
- Bug confirmed with reproduction steps
- Error in application code, not configuration
- Performance issue requiring code-level investigation
- Security vulnerability suspected

### Escalate to Management When:
- PR-sensitive situation (social media backlash, press inquiry)
- VIP/executive customer with unresolved issue
- Legal or compliance implication
- Repeated severity 1 or 2 incidents

## Incident Classification

| Severity | Description | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| SEV-1 | System-wide outage or data loss | Full platform unavailable, data corruption |
| SEV-2 | Major feature unavailable for many users | Payment processing down, search broken |
| SEV-3 | Minor feature issue, workaround available | UI bug on a secondary page, slow load on non-critical feature |
| SEV-4 | Cosmetic, documentation, feature request | Typo in UI, missing help article |

## Incident Response - SEV-1 / SEV-2

### Process
1. **Detect**: Automated monitoring alert OR customer report
2. **Acknowledge**: Incident Owner acknowledges within 5 minutes
3. **Communicate**: Post to status page within 10 minutes
4. **Triage**: Determine severity, assemble response team
5. **Mitigate**: Apply fix or workaround; prioritize restoring service
6. **Resolve**: Confirm service restored; update status page to "resolved"
7. **Post-mortem**: Root cause analysis within 48 hours (SEV-1) or 5 business days (SEV-2)

### Communication Templates

**Acknowledgment:**
> We are aware of an issue affecting [feature]. Our team is investigating. Updates will follow.

**Update (every 30 min for SEV-1, every 4 hours for SEV-2):**
> [Team] continues to work on [issue]. [Progress update]. Next update at [time].

**Resolution:**
> The issue affecting [feature] has been resolved. A full post-mortem will be shared within [timeframe].

## Post-Mortem Template

- **Incident ID**: [unique identifier]
- **Date & Duration**: [start time] - [end time]
- **Severity**: SEV-[1|2|3|4]
- **Impact**: [users affected, features impacted, financial impact]
- **Root Cause**: [what caused the incident]
- **Trigger**: [what detected/precipitated the incident]
- **Resolution**: [how was it fixed]
- **Timeline**: [key events with timestamps]
- **Action Items**: [preventive measures with owners and deadlines]

documents.title: Product Documentation Standards
documents.summary: Standards and templates for creating and maintaining product documentation
documents.body:
# Product Documentation Standards

## Overview

Consistent, high-quality product documentation reduces support volume by enabling self-service and improves customer satisfaction. All documentation must follow these standards.

## Documentation Types

| Type | Purpose | Audience | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Getting Started Guide | First-time user onboarding | New users | Product Marketing |
| Feature Reference | Complete feature documentation | All users | Product Team |
| API Reference | Technical API documentation | Developers | Engineering |
| Troubleshooting Guide | Common issues and fixes | All users | Support Team |
| Release Notes | What's new in each release | All users | Product Marketing |
| FAQ | Frequently asked questions | All users | Support Team |
| Integration Guide | Third-party integration setup | Technical users | Engineering |

## Writing Standards

### Tone & Style
- **Clear and direct**: Use active voice. "Click Save" not "The Save button should be clicked."
- **Task-oriented**: Focus on what the user wants to accomplish
- **Concise**: One idea per paragraph. Use bullet points for lists.
- **Inclusive**: Use gender-neutral language. Avoid jargon unless defined.

### Required Sections per Article
1. **Title**: Clear, descriptive, includes primary keyword
2. **Summary**: 1-2 sentences explaining what this article covers
3. **Prerequisites**: What the user needs before starting (permissions, accounts, data)
4. **Steps**: Numbered steps for procedures. Screenshots for key steps.
5. **Troubleshooting**: Common issues and their solutions
6. **Related articles**: Links to related documentation

### Formatting


# Title (H1)

## Summary
Brief description of the article.

## Prerequisites
- Permission required: [role]
- Account type: [free/pro/enterprise]

## Steps
1. Navigate to **Settings > Integrations**.
2. Click **Add Integration**.
3. Select the integration type.
4. Enter the required credentials.
5. Click **Save** to activate.

## Troubleshooting
- **Integration not appearing**: Verify the integration is enabled for your account tier.
- **Connection failed**: Check that credentials are correct and the third-party service is online.

## Related Articles
- [API Authentication Guide](/docs/api-auth)
- [Webhook Setup](/docs/webhooks)


## Review & Update Cycle

| Article Type | Review Cadence | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Getting Started Guides | Every release | Product Marketing |
| Feature References | When feature changes | Product Team |
| API Reference | When API changes | Engineering |
| Troubleshooting Guides | Monthly | Support Team |
| Release Notes | Every release | Product Marketing |
| FAQ | Quarterly | Support Team |

## Quality Metrics

| Metric | Target |
|---|---|
| Documentation coverage (% of features documented) | > 95% |
| Article accuracy (self-reported correctness) | > 98% |
| Customer satisfaction with docs (CSAT) | > 90% |
| Time to find answer | < 2 minutes |
| Self-service resolution rate | > 60% |

documents.title: Customer Communication Templates
documents.summary: Standardized email and chat templates for common customer communications
documents.body:
# Customer Communication Templates

## Overview

Standardized communication templates ensure consistent, professional, and efficient customer interactions. Adapt templates as needed while maintaining the core structure and tone.

## Template Usage Guidelines

- Personalize every template with the customer's name and specific context
- Remove placeholder text before sending
- Keep the core structure intact
- Add case-specific details where appropriate
- When in doubt, add more empathy, not less

## Onboarding

### Welcome Email

**Subject**: Welcome to [Product Name]!

Hi [Customer Name],

Welcome to [Product Name]! We're excited to have you on board.

Here's what to do first:
1. **Complete your profile**: [Link to profile settings]
2. **Invite your team**: [Link to team management]
3. **Take the product tour**: [Link to product tour / getting started guide]
4. **Set up integrations**: [Link to integrations page]

Need help getting started? Our Knowledge Base has step-by-step guides for every feature.

Your dedicated support team is here if you need anything.

Best,
The [Product Name] Team

### First Call / Demo Follow-up

**Subject**: Great chatting with you!

Hi [Customer Name],

Thanks for your time earlier. As promised, here's a summary of what we covered:

- **[Topic 1]**: [Brief summary]
- **[Topic 2]**: [Brief summary]
- **[Topic 3]**: [Brief summary]

**Next steps:**
- [Action item 1]: [Due date]
- [Action item 2]: [Due date]

I've also shared:
- [Link to relevant docs]
- [Link to recorded demo (if applicable)]

Let me know if you have any questions.

Best,
[Your Name]

## Support Interactions

### Issue Acknowledgment

**Subject**: We're looking into this - [Case #12345]

Hi [Customer Name],

Thanks for reaching out. We've received your report about [brief issue description] and our team is investigating.

**What to expect:**
- We'll provide an update within [SLA time]
- You'll receive a notification when there's progress
- If you have additional details to share, please reply to this email

We'll keep you posted.

Best,
[Support Team]

### Issue Resolved

**Subject**: [Case #12345] - Issue resolved

Hi [Customer Name],

The issue with [issue description] has been resolved. Here's what happened:

**Root cause**: [Brief explanation]
**Resolution**: [What was done to fix it]

If you continue to experience the issue, please reply to this email and we'll reopen the case. Otherwise, this case will be automatically closed in 72 hours.

We value your feedback - please take a moment to rate your support experience: [CSAT Survey Link]

Best,
[Support Team]

## Billing & Account

### Upcoming Payment Failed

**Subject**: Action needed: Payment failed

Hi [Customer Name],

We were unable to process the payment for your [Product Name] subscription.

**What happened**: [Reason for decline - insufficient funds, expired card, etc.]
**Amount due**: [$X.XX]
**Due date**: [Date]

To avoid any interruption to your service, please update your payment method within 7 days:
[Link to billing settings]

Need help? Check our Billing FAQ or reply to this email.

Best,
The [Product Name] Team

### Account Upgrade Confirmation

**Subject**: You've been upgraded to [Plan Name]!

Hi [Customer Name],

Your [Product Name] account has been upgraded to **[Plan Name]**.

**What's new:**
- [New feature 1]
- [New feature 2]
- [New feature 3]

**Next charge**: $[X.XX] on [Date]
**Updated billing**: [Link to billing settings]

Start exploring your new features: [Link to new features page]

Best,
The [Product Name] Team

## Feedback & Follow-up

### Post-Case Survey Request

**Subject**: How did we do?

Hi [Customer Name],

We recently helped you with [brief issue description]. We'd love to hear about your experience.

How satisfied were you with the support you received?

[Very Satisfied] [Satisfied] [Neutral] [Dissatisfied] [Very Dissatisfied]

Your feedback helps us improve. The survey takes less than 2 minutes.

Thanks for being a [Product Name] customer!

Best,
[Support Team]

### Churned Customer Re-engagement

**Subject**: We miss you, [Customer Name]

Hi [Customer Name],

It's been a while since you used [Product Name], and we wanted to check in.

Since you left, we've added:
- **[New feature 1]**: [Brief value proposition]
- **[New feature 2]**: [Brief value proposition]
- **[New feature 3]**: [Brief value proposition]

We'd love to have you back. Your old account is still here - just log in to pick up where you left off.

If there's anything we could have done differently, we'd genuinely like to hear about it. Just hit reply.

Best,
The [Product Name] Team

documents.title: Knowledge Base & Help Center Management
documents.summary: Best practices for managing a SaaS help center and knowledge base
documents.body:
# Knowledge Base & Help Center Management

## Overview

A well-maintained knowledge base is the most effective tool for reducing support volume and empowering customers. This document covers the structure, maintenance, and optimization of your help center.

## Help Center Structure

### Recommended Sections

1. **Getting Started** - Onboarding guides, account setup, first steps
2. **Product Guides** - Feature documentation by product area
3. **Troubleshooting** - Common issues and step-by-step fixes
4. **FAQs** - Frequently asked questions organized by topic
5. **API & Integrations** - Technical documentation for developers
6. **Release Notes** - What's new, changelog, migration guides
7. **Billing & Account** - Plans, payments, team management

### Article URL Structure


help.example.com/{section}/{article-slug}


Examples:
- help.example.com/getting-started/create-account
- help.example.com/troubleshooting/login-issues
- help.example.com/api/authentication

## Content Management

### Article Lifecycle
1. **Draft**: Written by assigned author
2. **Review**: Peer-reviewed for accuracy and clarity
3. **Publish**: Made live in the help center
4. **Monitor**: Track views, CSAT, and search relevance
5. **Update**: Revise when features change or issues emerge
6. **Archive**: Remove or redirect when no longer relevant

### Content Health Metrics
| Metric | Target | Action if Below Target |
|---|---|---|
| Article CSAT | > 90% | Revise for clarity and completeness |
| Search success rate | > 70% | Improve SEO, add synonyms, restructure |
| Self-service rate | > 60% | Add more articles for top support drivers |
| Abandonment rate | < 30% | Improve article quality and navigation |
| Freshness (updated < 6 months) | > 80% | Schedule updates for stale articles |

## SEO for Help Center

### On-Page SEO
- Title tag: Include primary keyword + " - [Product Name] Help"
- Meta description: 150-160 characters, includes keyword and value proposition
- H1: Primary keyword naturally included
- URL: Short, descriptive, hyphen-separated
- Images: Alt text with descriptive keywords
- Internal links: Link to related articles (3-5 per article)
- External links: Link to official documentation and trusted sources

### Common SEO Mistakes
- Duplicate content (similar articles on the same topic)
- Orphan pages (no internal links pointing to the article)
- Keyword stuffing
- Thin content (articles shorter than 300 words)
- Outdated articles without freshness signals

## Analytics & Optimization

### Key Metrics to Track
1. **Search queries**: What are customers searching for? Are they finding answers?
2. **Top articles**: Which articles get the most views? Most CSAT?
3. **Zero-result searches**: Searches that return no results = documentation gaps
4. **Article drift**: Articles that lose ranking or CSAT over time
5. **Support deflection**: Articles viewed before creating a support ticket

### Optimization Cycle
1. **Month 1**: Audit top 10 support drivers. Ensure each has a help article.
2. **Month 2**: Improve bottom 10 performing articles (low CSAT, high abandonment).
3. **Month 3**: Review zero-result search queries. Create new articles for common gaps.
4. **Repeat**: Continuous improvement cycle.

## Tools & Integrations

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Help center platform (Intercom, Zendesk, Freshdesk) | Article hosting and search |
| Analytics (Google Analytics, Mixpanel) | Usage tracking |
| Feedback widgets | Article-level CSAT |
| Search analytics | Query tracking and optimization |
| AI chatbot | Answer common questions instantly |
